description.narrative:
The project titled The Imarisha Kilimo Plus Project (TIK +) is a 12-month initiative aimed at building sustainable livelihoods through climate-smart agriculture, inclusive market systems, and policy advocacy. Implemented by Beacon of Hope (BOH) in partnership with Christian Aid Kenya (CAK), the project will operate in Dagoretti North and South Sub-Counties, Nairobi County, and directly benefit 150 smallholder farmers—60% women, 30% youth and 10% men. This proposal builds on the strong foundation laid during Phase 1 of The Imarisha Kilimo Project (TIK), which surpassed its target by reaching 130 smallholder farmers (108% of goal). Over 92% of participants adopted climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices, 80% reported increased vegetable production, and 65% engaged in value addition (primarily through kale powder production). Notably, women's financial empowerment increased by 75%, and 70% of beneficiaries were linked to local markets, with 20% gaining access to formal buyers.
The proposed project (Phase 2) seeks to scale and deepen these outcomes by promoting indigenous, drought-resistant crops (e.g., managu, cowpeas, amaranth), enhancing local value chains through processing, branding, and packaging, and expanding access to microcredit and digital marketplaces. The project also emphasizes policy engagement to reduce structural barriers for smallholder farmers, such as lack of subsidies, high tariffs, and stringent certification processes. Key interventions include: Training 150 farmers in CSA techniques, composting, and organic pest control. Distribution of drought-resistant seed kits and irrigation tools. Establishment of six demonstration farms for peer learning. Support for Seven (7) VSLAs with training in record-keeping, savings mobilization, and credit access. Advanced training in value addition (e.g., vegetable drying, KEBS compliance) and e-commerce. Facilitation of market linkages with supermarkets, hotels, and exporters. Policy dialogues with government actors to advocate for pro-smallholder policies. The expected impact is substantial: 80% of farmers will adopt drought-resilient crops and CSA practices. 65% will participate in value-added processing. 70% will access formal and digital markets. 40% of VSLA members will secure microloans to grow their agri-businesses. At least one policy changes will be influenced at the county level. Sustainability is central to the project. BOH will guide farmer groups toward forming cooperatives and establishing a table banking initiatives from value-added sales to support future investments. Additionally, partnerships with government agencies and the private sector will be solidified through formal agreements, ensuring continued support beyond the project’s life cycle.
